sentences.text: Notice of the application stands issued vide order dated 07.07.2023.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the pleadings.
A perusal of the application shows that the applicants relied upon their co-sharers and gave their file to them for filing the appeal.
However, later on, it was found that no appeal was filed on behalf of the applicants, thereby causing the aforesaid delay in filing the appeal, which is apparently unintentional and bona fide.

Nonetheless, the other similarly situated landowners pertaining to the same acquisition proceedings have already been held entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation pertaining to Village Choma to the tune of Rs. 4,78,05,588/- per acre vide judgment dated 20.05.2016 passed by this Court in RFA No. 4475 of 2012, titled "Ram Chander and another Versus State of Haryana and others", though, it was reduced by 15% vide judgment dated 05.09.2017 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Civil Appeal No.11814-11864 of 2017.

Based thereupon, applying the principle of parity, the landowners / applicants being similarly situated, are entitled for grant of similar amount of compensation, however, without any payment of interest for the period they failed to approach this Court after the decision in the Reference Court.

In this regard reliance can be placed upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of "Ningappa Thotappa Angadi (Dead) through LRs Versus Special Land Acquisition Officer and Another", 2020 (19) SCC 599.

sentences.text: In view of the discussion made hereinabove, the present application is allowed and delay of 2221 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

MAIN APPEAL [1] Present appeal has been preferred under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (for short "the Act") to modify the impugned award dated 23.09.2014 passed by learned Additional District Judge, Gurgaon (hereinafter to be referred as "Reference Court") for enhancement of the compensation.

[2] The land owned by the applicants alongwith other co- villagers situated in Village Choma, District Gurugram was acquired vide Notification dated 25.01.2008 issued under Section 4 of the Act, which was followed by a declaration dated 18.03.2008 under Section 6 thereof.

The public purpose for acquisition of land was stated to be development and utilization of land for 150 meters wide periphery road linking 'Dwarka Township Delhi' from Haryana boundary.
3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:088648 RFA No. 794 of 2023 (O&M) 2023:
[3] The Land Acquisition Collector, Gurgaon (for short "LAC"), vide Award No. 66 dated 23.12.2009, assessed the market value of acquired land @ Rs. 60 lakh per acre.
[4] Dissatisfied with the aforesaid Award, landowners / interested persons filed objections under Section 18 of the Act.

Anoop Kumar Deceased Through His Lrs vs State Of Haryana And Others on 14 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50443789/
2
Resultantly, the dispute was referred to the Reference Court for determination of the market value of the acquired land.

[5] Learned Reference Court, while passing the impugned award dated 23.09.2014, accepted nine (09) reference petitions including the one filed by appellants and enhanced the compensation @ Rs. 1.84 crore per acre alongwith other statutory benefits.
The operative para-18 of impugned award is re

- produced as under:-
" 18.
As a sequel to my above detailed discussion on the aforesaid issues, I find merit in the 9 reference petitions mentioned in table No.2 above and the same are allowed with costs.
The victorious petitioners are held entitled to enhanced compensation at the rate of  1.84 core per acre for all kinds of land.
However, the 6 reference petitions mentioned in table No.1 are dismissed with costs.

Besides this, the victorious petitioners shall also get solatium at the rate of 30% as envisaged under sub section(2) of section 23 of the Act and as per provisions of section 23(1-A) of the Act,they shall also be entitled to an amount calculated at the rate of 12% per annum on the above mentioned assessed market value for the period commencing on and from the date of publication of notification under section 4 sub section (i) till the 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:088648 RFA No. 794 of 2023 (O&M) 2023:PHHC:088648 award of the Collector or the date of taking possession of the acquired land, whichever is earlier.

It is clarified that in case the possession of land has not been delivered to HSIIDC because of some stay order passed in some litigation initiated at the instance of petitioner, no interest would be payable for the period for which the stay is in operation.

They shall also be entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of taking possession for a period of one year and at the rate of 15% per annum after the date of expiry of the said period of one year till the payment is made as provided under section 28 of the Act.
They shall also be entitled to interest on the additional amount and solatium provided under sub sections (1-A) and (2) of Section 23 of the Act in accordance with law."

[6] A perusal of paragraph extracted hereinabove shows that the Reference Court enhanced the market value of acquired land from Rs. 60 lakh per acre to Rs.
1.84 crore per acre, besides statutory benefits.
Aggrieved thereof, the appellants have preferred the present appeal.

[7] Learned counsel for the parties are ad idem that the matters pertaining to the same acquisition/notification covering the same revenue estate i.e. Village Choma filed at the instance of few other land-owners came up before this Court which was disposed off vide judgment dated 20.05.2016 passed in RFA No. 4475 of 2016, titled "Ram Chander and another Versus State of Haryana and others", whereby they have already been held entitled for the enhanced amount of compensation 5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:088648 RFA No. 794 of 2023 (O&M)
2023:PHHC:088648 pertaining to Village Choma to the tune of Rs. 4,78,05,588/- per acre; though,
it was reduced by 15% vide judgment dated 05.09.2017 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Civil Appeal Nos. 11814-11864 of 2017 (arising out of SLP(C) Nos. 8024-8074 of 2017).
